fixes.explanation: Egypt it is, friend. The famine was severe, so Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while (Genesis 12:10). When the pantry runs low, people go looking for a place with food. That's a very human reason to pack up and head somewhere new.

Nobody's asking Abram anything here, friend. The officials "…commended her to him…" meaning to Pharaoh (Genesis 12:15). They went straight over Abram's head to the top. Abram doesn't even get a seat in that verse, he's the last to know.

Ooh, I see why you picked it, but no warning here. The officials "…commended her to him…" (Genesis 12:15). They spoke well of her to Pharaoh. If that was a warning, it was the nicest warning ever delivered. Nobody sends a warning with a smile and a recommendation letter!

A temple would be a whole different address, friend, but that's not what the text says. Sarai "…was taken into the palace of Pharaoh." (Genesis 12:15). Palace is the word. Temple is a fine guess, though, so no hard feelings.

That's the whole list, and it's a long one. Abram "…acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels." (Genesis 12:16) The same verse says Pharaoh treated Abram well on her account. My order forms never run that long, friend. I think this part of the story is heavy.

Close, friend, but no court seat here. Abram "…acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels." (Genesis 12:16) That's a whole lot of animals and servants. Abram walked out with a parade, but not a single chair at the king's table.
